title: After last-second win, UM fan in Nepal flood carries message of resilience - The Detroit News
description: After last-second win, UM fan in Nepal flood carries message of resilience  The Detroit News
publisher.title: The Detroit News
full_article:
A photograph of a University of Michigan fan in a sludged-out Nepalese building may speak volumes about the humanitarian spirit in the face of overwhelming tragedy.

Or it may speak volumes about the reach of university branding, or even about a controversial college football game broadcast around the world.

Whatever the case, the man, who is not identified, was photographed while talking on the phone Tuesday, Sept. 8, by Pedro Pardo for Agence France-Presse and distributed via Getty Images. Along with his UM hat, he wears a shirt that reads, "Never give up."

It's not clear if his wardrobe was a statement in the aftermath of tragedy, a last-minute grab with unintended irony or something else altogether. Either way, it's a testament to the reach of the Michigan brand and, just maybe, to the worldwide reach of U.S. college sports.

There's no question that an immense humanitarian struggle continues in Nepal, where the glacial and mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border Aug. 26 killed at least 1,398 people and 5,500 remain missing.

It's also possible that his garb references the controversial last-second victory over Western Michigan University in a nationally televised and worldwide streamed game on Saturday. Based on developments Tuesday, the game's outcome may still be in doubt.

The photo caption says only that the man sits inside a damaged and sludge-ridden house in the aftermath of the flash floods at Devighat in Nepal's Nuwakot district.

Whatever the case, the block 'M' and a message of resilience were on display in Nepal.

Here's a closer look:

The shirt appears to be by Hoooyi, a Chinese brand based in Hong Kong. It's hard to be sure, but the hat appears to be a Jordan brand block 'M' hat in beige.
translated:
कीचड़ स॑ भरलऽ नेपाली भवन म॑ मिशिगन विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ प्रशंसक केरऽ फोटो भारी त्रासदी के सामना करतें हुअ॑ मानवीय भावना के बारे म॑ बहुत कुछ बोल॑ सकै छै ।

या ई विश्वविद्यालय ब्रांडिंग केरऽ पहुँच के बारे म॑ बहुत कुछ बोल॑ सकै छै, या यहाँ तलक कि दुनिया भर म॑ प्रसारित एगो विवादित कॉलेज फुटबॉल खेल के बारे म॑ भी ।

जे भी हो, ई आदमी, जेकरऽ पहचान नै करलऽ गेलऽ छै, के फोटो मंगलवार, ८ सितंबर क॑ फोन प॑ बात करतें हुअ॑ एजेंसी फ्रांस-प्रेस लेली पेड्रो पार्दो न॑ खींचलकै आरू गेटी इमेजेज के माध्यम स॑ वितरित करलकै । यूएम टोपीक संग एकटा शर्ट पहिरने छथि जाहि पर लिखल अछि "कहियो हार नहि मानब."

ई स्पष्ट नै छै कि हुनकऽ अलमारी त्रासदी के बाद के बयान छेलै, अनचाहा विडंबना के साथ अंतिम समय के हड़पना छेलै या एकदम सें कुछ आरू । कोनो तरहें, ई मिशिगन ब्रांडक पहुँचक गवाही थिक आ, बस, शायद, अमेरिकी कॉलेजक खेलक विश्वव्यापी पहुँचक गवाही थिक.

एहि मे कोनो संदेह नहि जे नेपाल मे एकटा अपार मानवीय संघर्ष जारी अछि, जतय 26 अगस्त कए चीन-नेपाल सीमा पर हिमनदी आ पहाड़ी पतन मे कम सं कम 1398 लोकक मौत भ गेल आ 5500 लोक लापता अछि.

ई भी संभव छै कि हुनकऽ परिधान शनिदिन राष्ट्रीय स्तर प॑ टेलीविजन आरू दुनिया भर म॑ स्ट्रीम करलऽ गेलऽ खेल म॑ वेस्टर्न मिशिगन यूनिवर्सिटी प॑ आखिरी सेकंड के विवादित जीत के संदर्भ दै छै । मंगलदिन भेल घटनाक्रम के आधार पर एहि खेल के परिणाम पर एखनो संदेह भ सकैत अछि.

फोटो कैप्शन मे मात्र एतबे कहल गेल अछि जे नेपालक नुवाकोट जिलाक देवीघाट मे आयल आकस्मिक बाढ़िक बाद ओ आदमी क्षतिग्रस्त आ कीचड़ सँ भरल घरक भीतर बैसल अछि ।

जे होउ, नेपाल मे ब्लॉक ‘एम’ आ लचीलापनक संदेश प्रदर्शित छल ।

एहि ठाम एकर गहन नजरि देल गेल अछि:

ई शर्ट हांगकांग म॑ स्थित चीनी ब्रांड हूयी केरऽ लगै छै । ई तय करब मुश्किल अछि, मुदा टोपी बेज रंग मे जॉर्डन ब्रांड क ब्लॉक 'एम' टोपी बुझाइत अछि।

title: Medicines Arrive in Nepal as Health Providers Work to Reach the Last Mile - Direct Relief
description: Medicines Arrive in Nepal as Health Providers Work to Reach the Last Mile  Direct Relief
publisher.title: Direct Relief
full_article:
Medicines Arrive in Nepal as Health Providers Work to Reach the Last Mile

By Lara Cooper

Fourteen tons of requested medical aid arrived in Kathmandu, Nepal, over the weekend to support communities impacted by last month's flash floods.

More than 1,300 people were killed when catastrophic flooding swept through entire communities in northern Nepal and southern Tibet on August 26. More than 5,000 people are still missing, and more than 13,000 people have been rescued.

Medical aid from Direct Relief was pre-positioned in the country before the floods, allowing emergency response teams to deploy immediately and begin providing care. Additional requested support arrived in the country on Sept. 6 and will be distributed in coordination with Nepal's Ministry of Health and Population.

The shipment contains items to address medical needs, including antibiotics, IV fluids, medications for chronic disease management, water purification supplies, and personal protective equipment.

Direct Relief is also working with local organizations to distribute medical support and provide services to the last mile of the response, to communities where access remains limited or cut off due to infrastructure damage. One Heart Worldwide, the Shanti Foundation, Mountain Heart Nepal, and Dhulikhel Hospital all reported last week how they've been reaching communities, in spite of major access challenges.

More than 40 bridges have been washed away, leaving many communities with limited road access, particularly in Rasuwa district. That district’s road connection to Nuwakot district to the south, which borders Kathmandu, the country’s capital, has been severed. Crews are working to clear roads in order to install temporary bridges, and air support to remote areas continues. Roads that are still open have been challenging due to ongoing rains.

“It’s been a real race against time, because access is very difficult,” according to Gordon Willcock, Direct Relief's Regional Director of Asia Pacific Programs. Willcock was in Kathmandu to receive the recent infusion of medical aid and met with local organizations responding, including One Heart World Wide.

Surya Bhatta of One Heart Worldwide described the organization’s recent trip into affected areas to bring medical aid after “six or seven hours of off-roading from mountain to mountain,” he said. The organization was able to deliver requested medications to Trishuli Hospital in Nuwakot, as well as bring counselors to Rasuwa to provide psychological first aid to people in holding centers that have been displaced by the floods.

The organization shared a video of a delivery truck making its way through thick mud on the road from Galchi Dhading, the only road north, on the way to deliver aid to Trishuli Hospital in Nuwakot.

“The main highway that people used to travel is all gone now,” said Jagdishwor Upadhyay, also of One Heart Worldwide. An alternate route through Nuwakot “is a rural road,” not a regular highway, he said, and rains have caused even more degradation to the road. When the group arrived, Upadhyay said a counselor was able to connect with a woman who was six months pregnant. She lost her family members, as well as her life savings, and her home, he recounted. She was staying at the holding center, and One Heart Worldwide was able to connect her with nutrition, hygiene products, and also clothing.

“It’s a really small thing, but it means a lot,” he said.

One Heart Worldwide shared a video of people crossing the Trishuli River via zipline. Rains have continued in the area, and the river could be seen running below.

Another Direct Relief partner organization, the Shanti Foundation, reported last week that they had arrived in the Trishuli flood-affected areas in Tukuche, Nuwakot, which lies along the road to Rasuwa.

"We are traveling to Rasuwa via the Dhading Road," she reported, and local leaders reported that more than 600 people in the area had been swept away by the floods. The organization is providing support to women and children impacted by the disaster.

Mountain Heart Nepal reported last week that "we are focusing our response on Rasuwa, where little assistance has reached because of the difficult and treacherous road conditions. Much of the relief effort has understandably been concentrated in the more accessible parts of Nuwakot."

"We are delivering essential medicines and medical supplies to Jibjibe Primary Hospital and affected communities around Kalikasthan. We also moved oxygen concentrators from [Siddhasthali] hospital to Rasuwa, as the local hospital was struggling to care for patients with COPD and asthma due to a lack of oxygen cylinders and limited options for refilling them."

स्वास्थ्य प्रदाता सब अंतिम मील तक पहुंचय लेल काज करैत नेपाल मे दवाई पहुंचल

लारा कूपर द्वारा

पिछला मास के आकस्मिक बाढ़ि सं प्रभावित समुदाय के सहयोग के लेल सप्ताहांत मे नेपाल के काठमांडू मे 14 टन आग्रह कएल गेल चिकित्सा सहायता पहुंचल.

26 अगस्त कए उत्तरी नेपाल आ दक्षिणी तिब्बत मे पूरा समुदाय मे विनाशकारी बाढ़ि मे 1300 स बेसी लोक क मौत भ गेल छल।

बाढ़ स॑ पहल॑ देश म॑ डायरेक्ट रिलीफ स॑ मिलै वाला मेडिकल एड क॑ पूर्व-स्थापित करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ आपातकालीन प्रतिक्रिया टीम क॑ तुरंत तैनात करी क॑ देखभाल करना शुरू करी देलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । अतिरिक्त अनुरोधित सहयोग ६ सितम्बरके देशमे पहुँचल आ नेपालके स्वास्थ्य तथा जनसंख्या मन्त्रालयके समन्वयमे वितरण कएल जाएत ।

शिपमेंट मे चिकित्सा जरूरतक कें पूरा करय कें लेल आइटम शामिल छै, जइ मे एंटीबायोटिक, आईवी तरल पदार्थ, पुरानी बीमारी प्रबंधन कें लेल दवाई, जल शुद्धिकरण आपूर्ति, आ व्यक्तिगत सुरक्षा उपकरण शामिल छै.

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ स्थानीय संगठनक कें साथ मिल क चिकित्सा सहायता वितरित करय आ प्रतिक्रिया कें अंतिम मील तइक सेवा प्रदान करय कें लेल सेहो काज कयर रहल छै, ओय समुदायक कें जत बुनियादी ढाँचा कें नुकसान कें कारण पहुंच सीमित रहय छै या बंद भ गेल छै. वन हार्ट वर्ल्डवाइड, शांति फाउंडेशन, माउंटेन हार्ट नेपाल, आरू धुलिखेल अस्पताल सब न॑ पिछला सप्ताह रिपोर्ट करलकै कि कोना ई समुदायऽ तलक पहुँची रहलऽ छै, पहुँच केरऽ बड़ऽ चुनौती के बावजूद ।

40 स बेसी पुल बहल अछि, जाहि स बहुत समुदाय कए सड़क क पहुंच सीमित भ गेल अछि, खास क रसुवा जिला मे। ओहि जिला के दक्षिण में नुवाकोट जिला सं सड़क कनेक्शन जे देश के राजधानी काठमांडू के सीमा पर अछि, ओकरा टूटि गेल अछि. अस्थायी पुल लगाबै के चक्कर म॑ चालक दल सड़कऽ क॑ खाली करै के काम करी रहलऽ छै, आरू दूर-दराज के इलाका म॑ हवाई सहायता जारी छै । जे सड़क एखनो खुजल अछि ओ जारी बरखा के कारण चुनौतीपूर्ण रहल अछि.

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ केरऽ एशिया प्रशांत कार्यक्रम केरऽ क्षेत्रीय निदेशक गॉर्डन विलकॉक के अनुसार, “समय के खिलाफ ई एगो वास्तविक दौड़ रहलऽ छै, कैन्हेंकि पहुँच बहुत मुश्किल छै । विलकॉक हाल ही म॑ चिकित्सा सहायता केरऽ इंफ्यूजन लेली काठमांडू म॑ छेलै आरू एकरऽ जवाब दै वाला स्थानीय संगठनऽ स॑ भेंट करलकै, जेकरा म॑ वन हार्ट वर्ल्ड वाइड भी शामिल छेलै ।

हुनी कहलकै कि वन हार्ट वर्ल्डवाइड केरऽ सूर्य भट्ट न॑ संगठन केरऽ हाल केरऽ प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ के यात्रा के वर्णन करलकै ताकि “पहाड़ स॑ पहाड़ प॑ छह-सात घंटा के ऑफ-रोडिंग” के बाद चिकित्सा सहायता लानलऽ जाय सक॑ । संगठन नुवाकोट केरऽ त्रिशुली अस्पताल म॑ माँगलऽ गेलऽ दवाई पहुँचै म॑ सफल रहलै, साथ ही साथ काउंसलर क॑ रसुवा म॑ लानी क॑ होल्डिंग सेंटर म॑ मौजूद लोगऽ क॑ मनोवैज्ञानिक प्राथमिक चिकित्सा उपलब्ध करै म॑ सफल रहलै जे बाढ़ स॑ विस्थापित होय गेलऽ छै ।

संस्था न॑ नुवाकोट केरऽ त्रिशुली अस्पताल म॑ सहायता पहुँचै के रास्ता म॑ उत्तर केरऽ एकमात्र सड़क गलची धडिंग स॑ सड़क प॑ मोटऽ कीचड़ स॑ गुजरत॑ एगो डिलीवरी ट्रक के वीडियो शेयर करलकै ।

वन हार्ट वर्ल्डवाइड केरऽ भी जगदीश्वर उपाध्याय न॑ कहलकै कि जे मुख्य राजमार्ग प॑ लोगऽ के यात्रा करलऽ जाय छेलै, वू अब॑ सब खतम होय गेलऽ छै । ओ कहलनि जे, नुवाकोट सं होइत वैकल्पिक मार्ग “ग्रामीण सड़क” अछि, नियमित राजमार्ग नहिं, आ बरखा के कारण सड़क के आओर बेसी गिरावट आयल अछि. ग्रुप पहुंचला पर उपाध्याय कहला जे एकटा काउंसलर छह मासक गर्भवती महिला स जुड़बा मे सफल रहल। ओ अपन परिवारक सदस्यक संग-संग जीवनक बचत, आ घर सेहो गमा लेलनि, ओ बतौलनि। ओ होल्डिंग सेंटर में रहैत छलीह, आ वन हार्ट वर्ल्डवाइड हुनका पोषण, स्वच्छता उत्पाद, आ कपड़ा सं सेहो जोड़बा में सक्षम छल.

ओ कहलनि जे, ई सचमुच छोट बात अछि, मुदा एकर बहुत मतलब अछि।

वन हार्ट वर्ल्डवाइड न॑ जिपलाइन के माध्यम स॑ त्रिशुली नदी पार करै वाला लोगऽ के वीडियो शेयर करलकै । एहि इलाका मे बरखा जारी अछि, आ नीचा नदी बहैत देखल जा सकैत छल।

डायरेक्ट रिलीफ केरऽ एगो आरू भागीदार संगठन शांति फाउंडेशन न॑ पिछला सप्ताह खबर देल॑ छै कि हुनी रसुवा जाय वाला सड़क के किनारे स्थित नुवाकोट केरऽ तुकुचे म॑ त्रिशुली बाढ़ प्रभावित इलाका म॑ पहुँची गेलऽ छै ।

ओ रिपोर्ट केलनि जे, हम धडिंग रोड होइत रसुवा जा रहल छी, आ स्थानीय नेता सब के रिपोर्ट अछि जे एहि इलाका के 600 सं बेसी लोक बाढ़ि सं बह गेल अछि. ई संस्था आपदा स॑ प्रभावित महिला आरू बच्चा सिनी क॑ सहायता प्रदान करी रहलऽ छै ।

माउंटेन हार्ट नेपाल न॑ पिछला सप्ताह रिपोर्ट करलकै कि "हमरा सब अपनऽ प्रतिक्रिया रसुवा प॑ केंद्रित करी रहलऽ छियै, जहां सड़कऽ के कठिन आरू विश्वासघाती स्थिति के कारण बहुत कम सहायता पहुँचलऽ छै । राहत केरऽ बहुत प्रयास समझै योग्य छै कि नुवाकोट केरऽ अधिक सुलभ भाग म॑ केंद्रित छै ।"

"हम जिबजीबे प्राथमिक अस्पताल आ कालिकास्थान के आसपास प्रभावित समुदाय मे आवश्यक दवाई आ चिकित्सा सामान पहुंचा रहल छी।" हम ऑक्सीजन कंसेन्ट्रेटर सेहो [सिद्धस्थली] अस्पताल स रसुवा ल गेल, किया कि स्थानीय अस्पताल ऑक्सीजन सिलेंडर क कमी आ ओकरा फेर स भरबाक सीमित विकल्प क कारण सीओपीडी आ दमा क मरीज क देखभाल करबा मे संघर्षरत छल।"

title: South Jordan restaurant donates day's sales to Nepal disaster relief fund - KSL.com
description: South Jordan restaurant donates day's sales to Nepal disaster relief fund  KSL.com
publisher.title: KSL.com
full_article:
SOUTH JORDAN — As Nepal faces mounting devastation from deadly flooding and a new earthquake, a South Jordan restaurant is stepping up to help.

Bawarchi owner Prkash Shah pledged to donate 100% of the restaurant's sales Tuesday to Nepal's Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund, giving Utahns an opportunity to support those affected while enjoying a meal.

The fundraiser comes as Nepal continues to recover from catastrophic flash floods that have killed more than 1,300 people, with thousands more still reported missing. A new earthquake struck the region Tuesday, compounding challenges for rescue crews and survivors.

For Shah, the tragedy is deeply personal.

"I have family over there," he said.

Prkash Shah is pictured in his restaurant, Bawarchi, in South Jordan on Tuesday. (Photo: Istvan Bartos, KSL)

Shah said watching footage of the destruction has been difficult.

"I think it is very surreal, to say the least," he said. "It was almost like a scene from an epic fiction movie."

Customers throughout the day said they were eager to support the effort.

Miranda Westman stopped by Bawarchi to pick up lunch and said helping others was an easy decision.

"We thought, why not do a lunch today that's going to help some people in need?" Westman said.

Like many others, she has followed coverage of the disaster from afar.

"It's kind of unbelievable," she said. "You see the before-and-after pictures of different areas that had schools or villages or towns, and they're just gone."

Shah said he has already made a personal donation but wanted to do more.

"I donated personally, but if I can do more, then why not?" he said.

I think it is very surreal, to say the least. It was almost like a scene from an epic fiction movie," Prkash Shah, owner of Bawarchi.

Gajushre Stha, who has immediate family in Nepal, said his loved ones were not harmed. Still, he said the devastation has affected the entire country.

"The whole country is my family, you know," Stha said. "So it's heartbreaking."

The restaurant also planned live music as part of the fundraising event and encouraged community members to contribute, even if they could not stay for a meal.

Owners said donations would continue to be accepted throughout the event, with all proceeds benefiting relief efforts in Nepal.

title: Why Nepal is demanding climate justice and compensation after deadly floods - Al Jazeera
description: Why Nepal is demanding climate justice and compensation after deadly floods  Al JazeeraNepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster  The GuardianThe Danger of Ignoring Nepal  Time Magazine
publisher.title: Al Jazeera
full_article:
Nepal is demanding “climate justice” and $20m in compensation after the recent devastating floods in the country and China’s Tibet region, which led to the deaths and disappearances of thousands of people.

The catastrophe, which scientists say was caused by the effects of climate change, was triggered when part of a mountain glacier collapsed and a torrent of water and mud flooded down into Nepal’s Rasuwa and Nuwakot regions, as well as into China’s Tibet region on August 26. More than 1,300 people have been confirmed dead and more than 5,000 remain missing.

Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300

Photos: UN urges global aid after China, Nepal floods kill over 1,300 list 2 of 3 Nepal holds day of mourning for more than 1,300 killed in floods

Nepal holds day of mourning for more than 1,300 killed in floods list 3 of 3 ‘Limit overshoot, peak, decline’: A new global goal for climate change? end of list

“We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create,” Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said last week.

“Support for Nepal should not be seen from an angle of aid or charity, but should be seen from the perspective of climate justice,” he told the AFP news agency.

On Monday, the country’s President Ramchandra Paudel made a similar demand during an address to the nation.

“I make a heartfelt appeal to the international community not only to listen to the voices of ecologically vulnerable countries, including Nepal, but also to take concrete and effective steps to ensure climate justice for them,” he said.

Nepal’s Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Environment have written a joint letter to the United Nations, which set up a fund to respond to loss and damage caused by climate change in 2022 in line with the 2015 Paris Agreement on climate, with a request for $20m in damages.

The UN’s Loss and Damage Fund is, however, facing a $2.8bn funding gap as it prepares to approve its first climate recovery projects.

‘Collective frustration’

Nepal’s leaders may have a point.

Advertisement

Nepal contributes less than 0.1 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions and generates most of its electricity from renewable sources of energy. Yet its geographical location in the Himalayas makes it particularly vulnerable to severe climate and weather events.

Last month’s catastrophic flooding in the country comes against a backdrop of rapid global warming and glacial loss across the Himalayas.

Glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya mountain range – which spans Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, Nepal and Pakistan – lost ice 65 percent faster between 2011 and 2020 than during the previous decade.

Nepal’s glaciers, which are sandwiched between two major carbon emitters – India and China – have lost close to one-third of their ice volume in roughly three decades due to global warming, the United Nations said in 2023.

Tanuja Pandey, a Nepal-based climate activist and lawyer, said there is collective frustration behind Nepal’s demand for climate justice.

“People here feel the world often pays attention to Nepal only when a climate disaster becomes impossible to ignore. It is deeply painful to people here that global attention intensifies when headlines report thousands of people dead or missing and in the end, their suffering does not generate any urgency to fight climate change,” she told Al Jazeera.

Shreya KC, a 28-year-old Nepali climate activist, said there is profound anger and sadness among people in Nepal who say that they must no longer continue to suffer the impact of climate change, which, as they see it, other countries are responsible for.

“My hometown is in Solukhumbu in eastern Nepal,” the activist told Al Jazeera. “It is a district of mountains and is also home to the world’s highest mountain, Mount Everest, and my home is also downstream. After the glacial collapse happened two weeks ago, people in my region have realised that this can now happen anywhere in Nepal since the Himalayas are warming and glaciers are melting faster.”

While Nepal has been actively fighting climate change, Shreya KC said she herself has been involved in projects in the country that focus on clean hydropower generation, forestry and other such climate advocacy programmes.

“Because of other countries,” she said, “today Nepalis are the ones most impacted by climate change. So people want justice.”

[Planet Labs PBC]

Is there such a thing as ‘climate justice’?

According to preliminary estimates from Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, the country’s property, housing and infrastructure losses in the floods amount to some $2.56bn.

Advertisement

But claiming compensation under a notion of “climate justice” won’t be straightforward, according to Joyeeta Gupta, a professor of Environment and Development in the Global South at the University of Amsterdam.

According to the United Nations, “‘climate justice’ is the moral and ethical principle that seeks to address the disproportionate impact of climate change on vulnerable communities and future generations”.

“I define it as a system of justice where others’ perspectives are taken into account, and no harm is caused to others,” Gupta told Al Jazeera.

Nepal is a country that has very low emissions, she said, but is facing the brunt of climate issues which it never created. “That is reason enough for Nepal to claim climate justice,” she noted.

But, practically speaking, can it? In the pre-1990 period, there was a lot of discussion among nations about the need for large emitters to compensate those that would be harmed, Gupta noted. But soon after that, the term “compensation” disappeared from the agenda of international climate treaties, which turned more to discussions about providing assistance to developing countries that need to tackle climate change instead.

In a July 2025 advisory opinion on climate change, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) declared that “all nations have binding legal duties under international law to prevent significant climate harm”.

The ICJ’s advisory opinion on climate change also says that states breaching their international climate obligations can be required to make full reparations, including financial compensation to “injured states” or countries impacted by climate change caused by the actions of other countries.

While the ICJ’s opinion is not legally binding, Gupta said, it is a statement in international law that could support Nepal’s government’s international appeal for climate justice and compensation.

‘No climate justice without internal justice’

Nepal’s rapper-turned-prime minister, Balendra Shah, is scheduled to travel to New York on September 22 to address the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on September 24. His country’s appeal for climate justice is expected to be a key part of his address.

For climate activist Shreya KC, while UN meetings and international conferences on climate change may hold some weight when it comes to discussing climate disasters, right now, what Nepal needs is money.

“So much of our money allotted for healthcare, education and to transition into a more developed nation is now being spent on fighting climate change. So countries who are causing emissions, especially from the global north, need to commit more money to the UN’s Loss and Damage Fund,” she said, adding that money from that fund should be disbursed to vulnerable communities in need, not as a loan but as compensation for bearing the brunt of climate change.

Pandey noted that this is not the first time a climate disaster has occurred in Nepal and said that the new government, which came into power in March this year on the back of Nepal’s Gen Z protests last year, has also failed to make climate a priority in its budget.

Advertisement

While it is a good sign that Nepali politicians are appealing for international climate justice, she said, they also need to address the country’s internal development model to fight climate change in the first place.

“There is no climate justice without internal justice within the country itself,” she said.

“I hope that even in our development, partners and investors stop treating climate resilience as an optional addition to development in Nepal just because we are economically vulnerable.

“Investing in Nepal without investing in sustainability is simply a bad investment.”

On Monday, Nepal declared a national day of mourning to remember the more than 1,300 people who are known to have died in last month’s catastrophic floods. Thousands more are still missing.

The country’s President Paudel used the opportunity to call on people to unite.

“This is not a time for division. Nor is it a time to blame one another or become entangled in political disputes and confrontation,” he said.

“This is a time to demonstrate national unity and solidarity. It is also a time for reconstruction, rehabilitation and economic recovery.”

But Gupta says Nepal’s biggest challenge right now is establishing a precedent for compensation for climate change-related disasters.

“It was recently a glacial collapse in the country, but soon, it will become a bigger issue as time goes on because the monsoon patterns will change, the sea level will rise,” she said.

As many other developing countries – notably island states that face being submerged altogether – are also likely facing similar climate change challenges, the damage could become huge.

“That is going to be a very big reason why many rich countries will probably be unwilling to pay compensation, because that would set a precedent for future issues,” Gupta said.

“But the issues countries like Nepal are facing are a very strong argument to try and convince the whole world to accelerate action to phase out fossil fuels and fight climate change.”

वैज्ञानिकऽ के कहना छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन के प्रभाव के कारण ई प्रलय तखनिये शुरू होलै जब॑ 26 अगस्त क॑ पहाड़ी ग्लेशियर के कुछ हिस्सा गिरी गेलै आरू पानी आरू कीचड़ के धार नेपाल केरऽ रसुवा आरू नुवाकोट क्षेत्र के साथ-साथ चीन केरऽ तिब्बत क्षेत्र म॑ भी गिरी गेलै ।

नेपाल मे बाढ़ि मे 1300 स बेसी मृतक के शोक दिवस आयोजित सूची 3 of 3 ‘सीमा ओवरशूट, पीक, डिक्लाइन’: जलवायु परिवर्तन के लेल एकटा नव वैश्विक लक्ष्य? सूची के अंत

नेपाल के विदेश मंत्री शिसिर खनाल पिछला सप्ताह कहलनि जे, हम जे वैश्विक संकट के अंतिम कीमत चुका रहल छी जे हम सब नहि बनौने छी।

ओ एएफपी समाचार एजेन्सी स बातचीत मे कहलनि जे, नेपाल के समर्थन के सहायता या दान के कोण स नहि देखबाक चाही, बल्कि जलवायु न्याय के दृष्टिकोण स देखबाक चाही।

सोमदिन देश के राष्ट्रपति रामचंद्र पौडेल सेहो राष्ट्र के संबोधन के दौरान एहने मांग केलखिन्ह.

ओ कहलनि जे, हम अंतरराष्ट्रीय समुदाय स हृदय स अपील करैत छी जे नेपाल सहित पारिस्थितिकी क दृष्टि स कमजोर देश क आवाज सुनबा लेल नहि, बल्कि हुनका लेल जलवायु न्याय सुनिश्चित करबा लेल ठोस आ प्रभावी कदम उठाबय।

नेपाल केरऽ वित्त मंत्रालय आरू पर्यावरण मंत्रालय न॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र क॑ संयुक्त पत्र लिखलकै, जेकरा म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन प॑ २०१५ केरऽ पेरिस समझौता के अनुरूप २०२२ म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ होय वाला नुकसान आरू नुकसान के जवाब दै लेली एगो कोष के स्थापना करलऽ गेलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ २० मिलियन डॉलर के नुकसान के भरपाई के आग्रह करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

हालांकि संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ नुकसान आरू क्षति कोष क॑ २.८ अरब डॉलर के फंडिंग अंतर के सामना करना पड़॑ छै, कैन्हेंकि वू अपनऽ पहिलऽ जलवायु वसूली परियोजना क॑ मंजूरी दै के तैयारी करी रहलऽ छै ।

‘सामूहिक कुंठा’ २.

नेपाल’क नेता लोकनिक कोनो बात भ’ सकैत अछि.

विज्ञापन

नेपाल वैश्विक ग्रीनहाउस गैस उत्सर्जन मे 0.1 प्रतिशत सँ कम योगदान दैत अछि आ अपन अधिकांश बिजली नवीकरणीय ऊर्जा स्रोत सँ उत्पन्न करैत अछि । तइयो हिमालय में एकर भौगोलिक स्थिति एकरा भयंकर जलवायु आ मौसमी घटना के विशेष रूप स कमजोर बना दैत अछि ।

पिछला महीना देश म॑ आबी गेलऽ भयावह बाढ़ पूरा हिमालय म॑ तेजी स॑ ग्लोबल वार्मिंग आरू ग्लेशियल नुकसान के पृष्ठभूमि म॑ आबी रहलऽ छै ।

हिन्दू कुश हिमालय पर्वत श्रृंखला केरऽ पूरा ग्लेशियर – जे अफगानिस्तान, बांग्लादेश, भूटान, चीन, भारत, म्यांमार, नेपाल आरू पाकिस्तान म॑ फैललऽ छै – न॑ २०११ आरू २०२० के बीच पिछला एक दशक के तुलना म॑ ६५ प्रतिशत तेजी स॑ बर्फ के नुकसान करलकै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र न॑ २०२३ म॑ कहलकै कि दू प्रमुख कार्बन उत्सर्जक देशऽ – भारत आरू चीन – के बीच सैंडविच करलऽ गेलऽ नेपाल केरऽ ग्लेशियर म॑ ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के वजह स॑ लगभग तीन दशक म॑ अपनऽ बर्फ के मात्रा के लगभग एक तिहाई नुकसान होय गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल के जलवायु कार्यकर्ता आ वकील तनुजा पाण्डेय कहलनि जे, नेपाल के जलवायु न्याय के मांग के पाछु सामूहिक कुंठा अछि।

अल जजीरा स बातचीत मे ओ कहलीह जे एहि ठामक लोक कए लगैत अछि जे दुनिया प्रायः नेपाल पर तखने ध्यान दैत अछि जखन कोनो जलवायु आपदा कए नजरअंदाज करब असंभव भ जाइत अछि, एहि ठामक लोक लेल इ गहींर कष्टदायक अछि जे जखन हेडलाइन मे हजारों लोक क मौत या लापता हेबाक सूचना भेटैत अछि तखन वैश्विक ध्यान तेज भ जाइत अछि आ अंत मे हुनकर दुख स जलवायु परिवर्तन स लड़बाक कोनो तात्कालिकता नहि उत्पन्न होइत अछि।

नेपाली जलवायु कार्यकर्ता २८ वर्षीय श्रेया केसी कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे एहन लोक मे गहींर आक्रोश आ उदासी अछि जे कहैत छथि जे आब जलवायु परिवर्तनक प्रभाव हमरा लोकनि केँ नहि भोगैत रहबाक चाही, जकर जिम्मेवारी हुनका लोकनि केँ देखबा मे आन देश अछि।

कार्यकर्ता अल जजीरा केँ कहलनि जे, हमर सासुर पूर्वी नेपालक सोलुखुम्बु मे अछि। “ई पहाड़ केरऽ जिला छेकै आरू ई दुनिया केरऽ सबसें ऊँचऽ पहाड़ माउंट एवरेस्ट केरऽ घर भी छै, आरू हमरऽ घर भी नीचे के तरफ छै । दू सप्ताह पहलें हिमनदी केरऽ पतन के बाद हमरऽ क्षेत्र केरऽ लोगऽ क॑ ई अहसास होय गेलऽ छै कि ई अब॑ नेपाल म॑ कतहीं भी होय सकै छै, कैन्हेंकि हिमालय गरम होय रहलऽ छै आरू ग्लेशियर तेजी स॑ पिघली रहलऽ छै ।”

नेपाल जलवायु परिवर्तन स सक्रिय रूप स लड़ैत आबि रहल अछि, श्रेया केसी स्वयं देश मे स्वच्छ जलविद्युत उत्पादन, वानिकी आ अन्य एहन जलवायु वकालत कार्यक्रम पर केन्द्रित परियोजना मे संलग्न रहल बतौलनि।

ओ कहलीह जे अन्य देश क कारण आइ जलवायु परिवर्तन स सबस बेसी प्रभावित नेपाली छथि। तेँ लोक न्याय चाहैत अछि।”

[प्लैनेट लैब्स पीबीसी]।

‘जलवायु न्याय’ नामक कोनो बात छैक की ?

नेपाल के राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करय आ प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण के प्रारंभिक अनुमान के अनुसार बाढ़ में देश के संपत्ति, आवास आ बुनियादी ढांचा के नुकसान करीब 2.56 अरब डॉलर के अछि.

विज्ञापन

लेकिन एम्स्टर्डम विश्वविद्यालय केरऽ ग्लोबल साउथ म॑ पर्यावरण आरू विकास केरऽ प्रोफेसर जोयीता गुप्ता के अनुसार “जलवायु न्याय” केरऽ धारणा के तहत मुआवजा के दावा करना सीधा नै होतै ।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र के अनुसार, “‘जलवायु न्याय’ नैतिक आरू नैतिक सिद्धांत छै जे जलवायु परिवर्तन के कमजोर समुदाय आरू भविष्य के पीढ़ियऽ प॑ असमान प्रभाव क॑ संबोधित करै के कोशिश करै छै” ।

गुप्ता न॑ अल जजीरा स॑ कहलकै कि हम्में एकरा न्याय केरऽ एगो ऐसनऽ व्यवस्था के रूप म॑ परिभाषित करै छियै, जेकरा म॑ दोसरऽ के नजरिया क॑ ध्यान म॑ रखलऽ जाय छै, आरू दोसरऽ क॑ कोय नुकसान नै पहुँचै छै ।

नेपाल एकटा एहन देश अछि जकर उत्सर्जन बहुत कम अछि, मुदा जलवायु संबंधी मुद्दा के बोझ के सामना करय पड़ि रहल अछि जे ओ कहियो नहि पैदा केलक। ओ टिप्पणी केलनि जे, नेपाल लेल जलवायु न्यायक दावा करबाक लेल इएह काफी कारण अछि।

मुदा, व्यावहारिक रूपें, की भ' सकैत अछि? गुप्त न॑ नोट करलकै कि 1990 स॑ पहल॑ के दौर म॑ राष्ट्रऽ के बीच बहुत चर्चा होय गेलऽ छेलै कि बड़ऽ उत्सर्जकऽ के जरूरत छै कि जेकरा स॑ नुकसान होतै, ओकरा मुआवजा देलऽ जाय सक॑ । लेकिन ओकरऽ तुरंत बाद अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलवायु संधि केरऽ एजेंडा स॑ “मुआवजा” शब्द गायब होय गेलै, जेकरा म॑ विकासशील देशऽ क॑ सहायता दै के चर्चा म॑ बेसी बदलाव आबी गेलै, जेकरा बदला म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ निपटै के जरूरत छै ।

जलवायु परिवर्तन पर जुलाई २०२५ म॑ देलऽ गेलऽ सलाहकार राय म॑ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय न्यायालय (आईसीजे) न॑ घोषणा करलकै कि “सब राष्ट्रऽ प॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय कानून के तहत बाध्यकारी कानूनी कर्तव्य छै ताकि जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ महत्वपूर्ण नुकसान नै होय सक॑” ।

जलवायु परिवर्तन पर आईसीजे केरऽ सलाहकार राय म॑ ई भी कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि अपनऽ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय जलवायु दायित्वऽ के उल्लंघन करै वाला राज्यऽ स॑ पूरा क्षतिपूर्ति करै के जरूरत पड़॑ सकै छै, जेकरा म॑ “घायल राज्यऽ” या अन्य देशऽ के कार्रवाई स॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ प्रभावित देशऽ क॑ आर्थिक मुआवजा देना भी शामिल छै ।

गुप्ता कहलनि जे, आईसीजे के राय कानूनी तौर पर बाध्यकारी नहि अछि, मुदा ई अंतरराष्ट्रीय कानून मे एकटा एहन बयान अछि जे जलवायु न्याय आ मुआवजा के लेल नेपाल सरकार के अंतरराष्ट्रीय अपील के समर्थन क सकैत अछि।

‘आन्तरिक न्याय के बिना कोनो जलवायु न्याय नहि’

नेपाल केरऽ रैपर स॑ प्रधानमंत्री बनलऽ बलेन्द्र शाह २४ सितंबर क॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र महासभा केरऽ ८१वां अधिवेशन क॑ संबोधित करै लेली न्यूयॉर्क जाय वाला छै ।उम्मीद छै कि हुनकऽ देश केरऽ जलवायु न्याय केरऽ अपील हुनकऽ संबोधन केरऽ एगो प्रमुख हिस्सा होतै ।

जलवायु कार्यकर्ता श्रेया केसी के लेलऽ जहाँ जलवायु आपदा के चर्चा के बात आबै छै त॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र के बैठक आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन प॑ अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सम्मेलन म॑ कुछ वजन भी होय सकै छै, लेकिन अभी नेपाल क॑ जे जरूरत छै, वू छै पैसा ।

“स्वास्थ्य सेवा, शिक्षा आरू अधिक विकसित राष्ट्र म॑ संक्रमण लेली आवंटित हमरऽ एतना पैसा अब॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ लड़ै प॑ खर्च होय रहलऽ छै । त॑ जे देशऽ न॑ उत्सर्जन पैदा करी रहलऽ छै, खास करी क॑ वैश्विक उत्तर स॑, ओकरा संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ नुकसान आरू क्षति कोष म॑ अधिक पैसा समर्पित करै के जरूरत छै ।’

पाण्डेय न॑ नोट करलकै कि नेपाल म॑ जलवायु आपदा ई पहलऽ बार नै छै आरू कहलकै कि पिछला साल नेपाल केरऽ जेन जेड विरोध के बाद ई साल मार्च म॑ सत्ता म॑ ऐलऽ नया सरकार भी अपनऽ बजट म॑ जलवायु क॑ प्राथमिकता म॑ नै रखलकै ।

विज्ञापन

नेपाली राजनेता सब अंतरराष्ट्रीय जलवायु न्याय के लेल अपील क रहल छथि ओतहि नीक संकेत अछि, मुदा पहिल बेर जलवायु परिवर्तन स लड़बा लेल देश के आतंरिक विकास मॉडल के सेहो संबोधित करय के जरूरत अछि।

ओ कहली जे देश क भीतर ही बिना आंतरिक न्याय क जलवायु न्याय नहि होइत अछि।

“हमरा आशा छै कि हमरऽ विकास म॑ भी भागीदार आरू निवेशक न॑ जलवायु लचीलापन क॑ नेपाल म॑ विकास म॑ वैकल्पिक जोड़ के रूप म॑ मानना बंद करी दै छै, खाली ई लेली कि हम्में आर्थिक रूप स॑ कमजोर छियै ।

“स्थायित्व मे निवेश केने बिना नेपाल मे निवेश करब मात्र एकटा खराब निवेश अछि।”

सोमदिन नेपाल पिछला मासक भयावह बाढ़ि मे मृत्यु भेल 1300 सँ बेसी लोक केँ मोन पाड़बाक लेल राष्ट्रीय शोक दिवस घोषित केलक अछि । हजारों आओर एखनो लापता अछि।

देश केरऽ राष्ट्रपति पौडेल न॑ ई मौका के इस्तेमाल करी क॑ लोगऽ क॑ एकजुट होय के आह्वान करलकै ।

ओ कहलनि जे, ई विभाजन के समय नहि अछि, आ ने एक दोसरा के दोषी ठहराबय के समय अछि या राजनीतिक विवाद आ मुठभेड़ मे उलझय के समय अछि।

ओ कहला जे इ राष्ट्रीय एकता आ एकजुटता क प्रदर्शन करबाक समय अछि। पुनर्निर्माण, पुनर्वास आ आर्थिक सुधारक सेहो समय अछि।”

लेकिन गुप्ता के कहना छै कि नेपाल के अभी सबसें बड़ऽ चुनौती जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ जुड़लऽ आपदा के मुआवजा के मिसाल कायम करना छै ।

ओ कहली जे हाल मे इ देश मे हिमनदी क पतन छल, मुदा जल्दिये, समय क संग इ एकटा पैघ मुद्दा बनत, किया कि मानसून क पैटर्न बदलत, समुद्र तल बढ़त।

जेना कि बहुत सारा अन्य विकासशील देश – खास करी क॑ द्वीपीय राज्य जेकरा पूरा तरह स॑ डूबला के सामना करना पड़॑ छै – क॑ भी संभावना छै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ ऐसनऽ ही चुनौती के सामना करना पड़॑ छै, ई लेली नुकसान बहुत बड़ऽ होय सकै छै ।

गुप्ता कहलनि जे, इ बहुत पैघ कारण बनय वाला अछि जे शायद बहुत रास अमीर देश मुआवजा देबय लेल तैयार नहि होयत, किया कि एहि सं भविष्य के मुद्दा के लेल एकटा मिसाल कायम होयत।

“मुदा नेपाल जैसनऽ देशऽ के सामने जे मुद्दा छै, वू एगो बहुत मजबूत तर्क छै कि पूरा दुनिया क॑ जीवाश्म ईंधन क॑ चरणबद्ध तरीका स॑ समाप्त करै आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन स॑ लड़ै लेली कार्रवाई म॑ तेजी लानै के कोशिश आरू मनाबै के कोशिश करलऽ जाय ।”

title: Nepal floods: Aid worker describes the scale of the disaster - Islamic Relief Worldwide
description: Nepal floods: Aid worker describes the scale of the disaster  Islamic Relief Worldwide
publisher.title: Islamic Relief Worldwide
full_article:
September 9, 2026 Nepal -

Islamic Relief is working with local partners to support people affected by the deadly flooding in Nepal.

Pragya Adhikari, an Islamic Relief aid worker, has been supporting distributions in Nuwakot — one of the worst-affected areas:

“The suffering I can hear and see is so tragic. Even three storey buildings are inundated with sand and debris, with the floods reaching 8 or 9 metres high.

“Many children have been orphaned as they were at school while the floods killed their parents. Other entire families are still missing – I heard of families of 24 and 30 people who are still unaccounted for.

“The level of flooding and trauma of people that have lost their family is something these communities have never seen before. I met an elderly man in his seventies who told me he’d never seen flooding like this in his lifetime. He said it’s at least four times bigger than even the most intense flood they can remember.

“Recovery will take a lot a lot of time. Some areas are still only accessible by helicopter, but we have to start debris clearance as quickly as possible.”

Islamic Relief’s response

Islamic Relief are coordinating with Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and District Disaster Management Committee (DDMC) to ensure our support reaches those who need it most.

So far, we have begun distributing 1,000 emergency shelter kits in Rasuwa District.

Each shelter kit includes essential items such as tarpaulins, blankets, pillows, and foam mattresses to help families meet their immediate needs.

Shelter kits contain essentials like blankets and pillows

Rescue operations are ongoing

Local authorities have confirmed that more than 1,300 people have been killed by the devastating floods that struck Nepal’s northern border on 26 August. More than 5,000 people are missing.

Widespread damage to roads, bridges and communication networks is hampering access to remote communities, creating significant challenges for the humanitarian response and leaving people exposed to continuing monsoon rains.

The ongoing heavy rain and the destruction of dozens of roads and bridges in the worst affected regions of Rasuwa and Nuwakot mean large trucks are unable to pass the blocked roads. Journeys that should take 4-5 hours are taking up to 15 hours.

Tens of thousands of people have had their lives ripped apart by the floods. Please help us to ease their suffering and provide lifesaving support. Donate to our Nepal Floods Emergency Appeal now.
translated:
इश्वी सन् २०२६ सितम्बर ९ तारिख नेपाल - ९.

इस्लामिक रिलीफ स्थानीय साझेदारक संग मिलिकय नेपालमे भेल घातक बाढ़िसँ प्रभावित लोककेँ सहयोग कऽ रहल अछि ।

इस्लामिक राहत सहायताकर्मी प्रज्ञा अधिकारी नुवाकोट म॑ वितरण के समर्थन करी रहलऽ छै — सबसें जादा प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ स॑ एक:

ओ कहला जे जे दुख हम सुनि सकैत छी आ देख सकैत छी ओ एतेक दुखद अछि, तीन मंजिला भवन मे सेहो बालु आ मलबा स भरल अछि, जाहि मे बाढ़ि 8 या 9 मीटर तक पहुंच गेल अछि।

ओ कहला जे बहुत बच्चा स्कूल मे जेना अनाथ भ गेल अछि, जखन कि बाढ़ि मे ओकर माता-पिता क मौत भ गेल। आन पूरा परिवार एखनो गायब अछि – 24 आ 30 लोकक परिवारक बारे मे सुनलहुं जे एखनो धरि बेहिसाब अछि।

“परिवार के गंवा चुकल लोक के बाढ़ि आओर आघात के स्तर एहन चीज अछि जे ई समुदाय पहिने कहियो नहि देखने छल. हमरा सत्तर के दशक के एकटा बुजुर्ग सं भेंट भेल जे हमरा कहलनि जे ओ अपन जीवन मे एहन बाढ़ि कहियो नहि देखने छलाह. ओ कहलनि जे ई कम सं कम चारि गुना पैघ बाढ़ि सं सेहो बेसी अछि जे हुनका याद अछि.

ओ कहला जे रिकवरी मे बहुत बहुत समय लागत। किछु इलाका मे एखनो केवल हेलीकॉप्टर स पहुंचल जा सकैत अछि, मुदा हमरा सब कए जल्दी स जल्दी मलबा क निकासी शुरू करय पड़त।”

इस्लामिक रिलीफ के प्रतिक्रिया

इस्लामिक रिलीफ नेपाल केरऽ राष्ट्रीय आपदा जोखिम कम करै आरू प्रबंधन प्राधिकरण (एनडीआरआरएमए) आरू जिला आपदा प्रबंधन समिति (डीडीएमसी) के साथ समन्वय करी रहलऽ छै ताकि ई सुनिश्चित करलऽ जाय सक॑ कि हमरऽ सहयोग वू लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै जेकरा एकरऽ सबसें जादा जरूरत छै ।

एखन धरि हम रसुवा जिला मे 1000 इमरजेंसी शेल्टर किट वितरण शुरू क देलहुं अछि।

प्रत्येक आश्रय किट मे आवश्यक वस्तुअक जेना तिरपाल, कंबल, तकिया, आ फोम गद्दा शामिल छै, जे परिवारक कें ओकर तत्काल जरूरतक कें पूरा करय मे मदद करतय.

शेल्टर किट मे कंबल आ तकिया जैना आवश्यक चीजक होयत छै

बचाव कार्य जारी अछि

स्थानीय अधिकारी सब पुष्टि केलक अछि जे 26 अगस्त के नेपाल के उत्तरी सीमा पर आयल विनाशकारी बाढ़ि मे 1300 सं बेसी लोक के मौत भ गेल अछि. पांच हजार स बेसी लोक लापता अछि।

सड़क, पुल आरू संचार नेटवर्क केरऽ व्यापक नुकसान दूरस्थ समुदायऽ तलक पहुँच म॑ बाधा पहुँचै छै, जेकरा स॑ मानवीय प्रतिक्रिया लेली महत्वपूर्ण चुनौती पैदा होय रहलऽ छै आरू लोगऽ क॑ लगातार मानसून केरऽ बारिश के सामना करना पड़॑ लगलऽ छै ।

जारी भारी बारिश आरू रसुवा आरू नुवाकोट केरऽ सबसें जादा प्रभावित क्षेत्रऽ म॑ दर्जनों सड़क आरू पुल केरऽ तबाह होय के मतलब छै कि बड़ऽ ट्रक अवरुद्ध सड़कऽ स॑ गुजरै म॑ असमर्थ छै । जे यात्रा मे 4-5 घंटा लागय के चाही ओहि मे 15 घंटा तक के समय लागि रहल अछि.

दसों हजार लोकक जान बाढ़ि मे फाटि गेल अछि। कृपया हुनकर दुख कम करय में मदद करू आ जीवन रक्षक सहयोग प्रदान करू। अखन हमर नेपाल बाढ़ आपातकालीन अपील मे दान करू।

title: Video of mosque withstanding Nepal floods manipulated from footage of 'miracle house' - Yahoo
description: Video of mosque withstanding Nepal floods manipulated from footage of 'miracle house'  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
Flash floods triggered by a glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 swept away entire settlements in the Himalayan region, but video purportedly showing a mosque withstanding the destructive waves is in fact manipulated footage of a home that miraculously survived the disaster. The video appears to have been manipulated with the help of AI, and Google Street View imagery shows the affected area in Hindu-majority Nepal did not contain a mosque.

"Believe it or not, whether you like it or not, many places of worship, homes, and schools belonging to Muslims survived the floods in Nepal," says Indonesian-language text superimposed on a TikTok video posted on August 31, 2026.

The video appears to show a mosque with an emerald green dome standing firm against raging muddy floodwaters.

Screenshot of the false post captured on September 9, 2026, with AI label and red X added by AFP

The video was also shared in similar TikTok posts after a high-altitude glacial collapse at the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26 triggered devastating floods that killed at least 1,400 people and left more than 5,840 still missing nearly two weeks later ( archived link).

"Every time disaster strikes, the house of Allah always stands firm," read a comment on one of the posts from Muslim-majority Indonesia, another said: "God is the greatest."

The tsunami-like glacial floods also destroyed more than 2,500 buildings in Nepal's Trishuli valley, according to an AFP computation of data from Europe's Copernicus observatory ( archived link). When partially damaged buildings are included, the proportion of structures affected rises to more than seven out of 10, underscoring the flood's violence as it tore through the valley.

As well as homes, the disaster destroyed roads and bridges, making it more difficult to deliver aid and search for the missing.

The circulating footage, however, has been manipulated with the help of AI.

'Miracle house'

A reverse image search on Google using keyframes from the falsely shared video led to a similar Instagram clip posted by Australian media outlet News.com.au on September 1 ( archived link).

Advertisement Advertisement #_R_1dea6m6l1dinpfiuqq5bH1_ { display: none; } @media screen and (max-width: 767.95px) { #_R_1dea6m6l1dinpfiuqq5bH1_ { display: flex; } iframe { max-width: 100vw; } }

"A mint-green house stood strong while devastating flash floods swept through Nepal," reads its caption, adding that follow-up reports confirmed the house did not subsequently succumb to the freezing waters and the family seen sheltering on an upper balcony was rescued safely.

Aside from the mosque, elements in the falsely shared video -- including a flag in the foreground and an adjacent structure -- match the Instagram clip.

Screenshot of the falsely shared video (L) and the Instagram clip, with corresponding features highlighted by AFP

A subsequent keyword search found the same video in the Reuters video database, credited to Rohit Nishad ( archived link).

Its video description says the footage was filmed in the Nuwakot region of Nepal's Bagmati Province on August 26.

Advertisement Advertisement #_R_1jea6m6l1dinpfiuqq5bH1_ { display: none; } @media screen and (max-width: 767.95px) { #_R_1jea6m6l1dinpfiuqq5bH1_ { display: flex; } iframe { max-width: 100vw; } }

AFP also took photos and videos of what has been dubbed the "miracle house" from different angles ( archived link).

A turquoise-green house, dubbed the "miracle house" stands tall amid sludge near Trishuli river in the aftermath of flash floods. Arun SANKARAFP

This footage matches Google Street View imagery of the area, but there is no sign of a mosque as depicted in the falsely shared video ( archived link).

Screenshot comparison of the falsely shared video (top left), the September 1 Instagram clip (bottom left) and Google Street View imagery, with similarities highlighted by AFP

The falsely shared video contains visual inconsistencies that indicate it may have been manipulated with AI, such as the splashing floodwaters not appearing to interact with the mosque and leaving no marks on its facade.

An analysis of the clip using Google's SynthID Detector detected invisible SynthID watermarks in the video, indicating it was manipulated with the help of its AI tools ( archived link).

Screenshot of results from Google's SynthID Detector

AFP has debunked other misinformation about the Nepal-Tibet floods.

title: 1st Korean search team sent to Nepal set to return home this week - Korea JoongAng Daily
description: 1st Korean search team sent to Nepal set to return home this week  Korea JoongAng Daily
publisher.title: Korea JoongAng Daily
full_article:
Korea's first disaster relief team sent to Nepal is preparing to return home this week, while the government works to dispatch a second team to continue searching for Korean nationals left unreachable by last month's flooding, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Wednesday.

The Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) will fly back to Korea as scheduled on Friday aboard a Korean Air Force KC-330 transport plane, the Foreign Ministry said in a press release.

The team was dispatched on Sept. 2 for what was originally planned as a 10-day mission.

The same aircraft, en route to Nepal to bring the team home, will first deliver relief supplies — including blankets, cold-weather clothing and tents — donated by Korean companies to nongovernmental organizations operating in the country, the ministry said.

"A second KDRT team is being prepared to continue search operations," the ministry said.

Further details, including its deployment timeline and whether its work will lean more toward search efforts or reconstruction support, are expected only after another meeting of the Public-Private Joint Emergency Relief Council, as required by law.

Separately, the government's joint rapid-response team and the Korean Embassy in Nepal will continue working closely with Nepalese authorities and carrying out other necessary work, including support for the families of Korean nationals who remain unreachable, the ministry added.

The relief effort follows a flash flood that struck Nepal's Rasuwa district on Aug. 26, hitting the Upper Trishuli-1 hydropower plant construction site operated by Korea South-East Power and Doosan Enerbility. Nine Korean nationals working at the site remain unreachable in the disaster's immediate aftermath, prompting Seoul to dispatch a rapid-response team, pledge $1 million in humanitarian aid and later send the KDRT to assist in the search.

कोरिया केरऽ पहिलऽ आपदा राहत दल नेपाल भेजलऽ गेलऽ ई सप्ताह घर वापसी के तैयारी करी रहलऽ छै, जबकि सरकार पिछला महीना केरऽ बाढ़ स॑ पहुँच नै पहुँचलऽ कोरियाई नागरिकऽ के खोज जारी रखै लेली दोसरऽ टीम भेजै के काम करी रहलऽ छै ।

विदेश मंत्रालय न॑ एगो प्रेस विज्ञप्ति जारी करी क॑ कहलकै कि कोरिया आपदा राहत टीम (केडीआरटी) शुक्रवार क॑ कोरियाई वायुसेना केरऽ केसी-३३० परिवहन विमान प॑ सवार होय क॑ कोरिया वापस उड़तै ।

टीम क॑ २ सितंबर क॑ वू लेली भेजलऽ गेलऽ छेलै जेकरा मूल रूप स॑ १० दिन के मिशन के रूप म॑ योजनाबद्ध करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

मंत्रालय न॑ कहलकै कि टीम क॑ घर लानै लेली नेपाल जाय वाला वही विमान सबसें पहल॑ कोरियाई कंपनी सिनी द्वारा देश म॑ संचालित गैर-सरकारी संगठनऽ क॑ दान करलऽ गेलऽ राहत सामान – जेकरा म॑ कंबल, ठंडा मौसम के कपड़ा आरू टेंट शामिल छै – पहुँचैलऽ जैतै ।

मंत्रालय कहलक जे, खोज अभियान जारी रखबा लेल दोसर केडीआरटी टीम तैयार कैल जा रहल अछि।

एकरऽ तैनाती के समय रेखा आरू एकरऽ काम खोज प्रयास या पुनर्निर्माण समर्थन के तरफ अधिक झुकतै कि नै, सहित आरू विवरण के उम्मीद सार्वजनिक-निजी संयुक्त आपातकालीन राहत परिषद केरऽ एगो आरू बैठक के बाद ही करलऽ जाय छै, जैसनऽ कि कानून के अनुसार आवश्यक छै ।

अलग-अलग सरकार के संयुक्त रैपिड रिस्पांस टीम आ नेपाल मे कोरियाई दूतावास नेपाली अधिकारी के संग मिलिकय काज करैत रहत आ अन्य आवश्यक काज करैत रहत, जाहि मे कोरियाई नागरिक के परिवार के सहयोग सेहो शामिल अछि जे अप्राप्य रहि गेल अछि।

कोरिया साउथ-ईस्ट पावर आ दूसन एनर्बिलिटी द्वारा संचालित अपर त्रिशुली-1 जलविद्युत संयंत्र निर्माण स्थल पर 26 अगस्त कए नेपालक रसुवा जिला मे आयल आकस्मिक बाढ़िक बाद ई राहत प्रयास कयल गेल अछि । आपदा के तुरंत बाद भी ई जगह प काम करै वाला नौ कोरियाई नागरिक तक पहुँच नै छै, जेकरा चलतें सियोल नँ रैपिड रिस्पांस टीम भेजलकै, 10 लाख डॉलर के मानवीय सहायता के वादा करलकै आरू बाद मँ केडीआरटी क खोज मँ सहायता लेली भेजलकै ।

title: Love for Nepalese delicacy began at 17,800 feet in the Himalayas - The Denver Post
description: Love for Nepalese delicacy began at 17,800 feet in the Himalayas  The Denver Post
publisher.title: The Denver Post
full_article:
Spending two months in Mount Everest base camp and on the mountain above, which I had the great fortune to experience in 1985, is full of beauty, challenge, exhaustion, inspiration, wonder and hardship. On a difficult day, nothing lifted my spirits quite like hearing our Sherpa cook announce that we would be having yak meat momos for dinner.

Those minced meat dumplings spiced with cumin, garlic and ginger were an occasional treat, greatly appreciated, even if the yak meat could be tough and gristly sometimes. Four decades later, whenever I dine at one of Denver’s Nepalese restaurants, an order of momos instantly transports me back to our base camp in the shadow of Everest, which soared 11,000 feet above us. The exterior of Yak and Yeti in Arvada. (Photo by Kristin Morin/Denver Post file)

That trip gave me a taste for other Nepalese specialities, too, which takes me to three Denver-area restaurants specializing in the food of Nepal and India: The Sherpa House in Golden, Yak and Yeti (Wheat Ridge, Arvada and Westminster) and Himchuli (RiNo and the Highlands).

I should add that the Everest trip also gave me a deep fondness for the people of Nepal, renowned for their sweet friendliness and cheerfulness. I never knew people with so little in the way of material possessions could be so happy.

Khagendra Gurung, who owns the two Himchuli locations, grew up in Katunje, a village located on a trekking route 50 miles northwest of the Nepalese capital of Kathmandu. When trekkers from the U.S. passed through, they seemed friendly to him, and he began to dream about emigrating to America.

“I feel like the United States was different. I wanted to go there,” he said.

So he did, when he was in his mid-20s, joining a sister who lived in Nederland. He went to work at a Nepalese restaurant there.

Five years later, in 2007, he opened his own restaurant near Evergreen in Bergen Park, called Cuisine of the Himalayas. In 2016, he opened the first Himchuli in Denver’s Highland neighborhood. Five years later, he added the RiNo location. He still owns the Bergen Park restaurant and lives in Evergreen.

“I love Colorado, I love the people,” he said. “Colorado kind of seems like Nepal, the people are friendly. I love the mountains. That’s why I am not missing Nepal very much. Colorado feels like Nepal, you can see the mountains, you can hike trails.”

Related Articles Sherpa House brings taste, aroma of Himalayas to Golden | Opinion

Himchuli means “snowy peak,” by the way.

Khagendra is quite the entrepreneur, too. In addition to his Nepalese restaurants, he also owns Pizza Alley, located next door to the Highland Himchuli location, which serves New York-style pizza.

If you are unfamiliar with Nepali food, all three of the restaurants mentioned here — Himchuli, Sherpa House, Yak and Yeti — have buffets so you can sample different dishes.

The Arvada Yak and Yeti location occupies a Victorian-era mansion dating back to 1864 and is located three blocks from Olde Town Arvada. The Sherpa House, which is also located in a historic building, is located two blocks from downtown Golden. Owner Lhakpa Sherpa has developed the property into a cultural center for Front Range Nepalis. Sherpa House Restaurant and Culture Center in Golden, Colorado on Tuesday, Jan. 28, 2025. (Photo by Hyoung Chang/The Denver Post)

For me, there’s just something special about the aroma whenever I walk into a Nepalese restaurant, breathing in those pungent scents of garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and turmeric. It’s intoxicating.

In fact, before sitting down to write this piece, I couldn’t resist calling the Yak and Yeti in Arvada for a takeout lunch order of chicken momos, which they serve with a delicious Indian chutney dipping sauce. It brought back lots of memories, as it always does.

माउंट एवरेस्ट बेस कैंप आ ऊपरक पहाड़ पर दू मास बिताब, जकर अनुभव करबाक हमरा 1985 में बहुत सौभाग्य भेटल छल, सौन्दर्य, चुनौती, थकान, प्रेरणा, आश्चर्य आ कठिनाई सं भरल अछि. कठिन दिन में हमर सबहक शेर्पा रसोइया के घोषणा सुनब जे हम सब राति के भोजन में याक मीट मोमो खाएब, तहिना किछुओ हमर मनोबल के ओहिना नहि उठौलक।

जीरा, लहसुन आ अदरक के मसाला वाला ओ कीमा मांस के पकौड़ी बीच-बीच में भेटैत छल, बहुत सराहल जाइत छल, भले याक के मांस कखनो काल कठोर आ किरकिरी भ सकैत छल. चारि दशकक बाद जखन कखनो डेनवरक कोनो नेपाली रेस्टोरेंटमें भोजन करैत छी तं मोमोक ऑर्डर तुरंत हमरा सब सं 11 हजार फीट ऊपर उड़ल एवरेस्टक छायामें हमरा लोकनिक बेस कैंपमें ल’ जाइत अछि. अरवाड़ा मे याक आ यति के बाहरी भाग। (फोटो क्रिस्टिन मोरिन/डेनवर पोस्ट फाइल)

ओहि यात्रा सं हमरा आन नेपाली विशेषताक स्वाद सेहो भेटल, जे हमरा नेपाल आ भारतक भोजनक विशेषज्ञ तीन टा डेनवर-क्षेत्रक रेस्टोरेंटमें ल जाइत अछि : गोल्डनमें शेर्पा हाउस, याक आ येती ( गहूम रिज, अरवाडा आ वेस्टमिंस्टर ) आ हिमचुली ( रिनो आ हाईलैंड्स ).

हमरा इहो जोड़बाक चाही जे एवरेस्ट यात्रा हमरा नेपालक लोकक प्रति सेहो गहींर स्नेह देलक, जे मधुर मित्रता आ हँसमुखताक लेल विख्यात छल । हम कहियो नहि जनैत छलहुँ जे भौतिक सम्पत्तिक रास्ता मे एतेक कम लोक एतेक खुश भ' सकैत अछि.

हिमचुली दूनू स्थानक मालिक खगेन्द्र गुरुङ नेपालक राजधानी काठमांडू सँ ५० मील उत्तर पश्चिम मे ट्रेकिंग मार्ग पर स्थित गाम कातुन्जे मे पलल-बढ़ल अछि । जखन अमेरिका सं ट्रेकर्स ओहि सं गुजरलनि तं हुनका लोकनि कें दोस्ताना बुझाइत छलनि, आ हुनका अमेरिका प्रवास करबाक सपना देखय लगलाह.

ओ कहलनि जे, हमरा लगैत अछि जे अमेरिका अलग छल, हमरा ओतय जेबाक इच्छा छल।

त' ओ केलनि, जखन ओ 20 के दशक के मध्य मे छलाह, एकटा बहिन सं जुड़ि गेलाह जे नेदरलैंड मे रहैत छलीह. ओतय एकटा नेपाली रेस्टोरेंट मे काज करय लेल गेलाह.

पांच साल बाद 2007 मे बर्गन पार्क मे एवरग्रीन क समीप अपन रेस्टोरेंट खोललथि, जेकर नाम छल Cuisine of the Himalayas । 2016 मे डेनवर के हाईलैंड मोहल्ला मे पहिल हिमचुली खोललखिन्ह. पांच साल बाद ओ रिनो लोकेशन कए जोड़ि देलथि। एखनो बर्गन पार्क रेस्टोरेंट के मालिक छथि आ एवरग्रीन में रहैत छथि.

ओ कहलनि जे, हमरा कोलोराडो स प्रेम अछि, हम लोक स प्रेम करैत छी। “कोलोराडो एक तरहेँ नेपाल जकाँ लगैत अछि, लोक मिलनसार अछि। हमरा पहाड़ बहुत नीक लगैत अछि। ताहि लेल हमरा नेपालक बेसी कमी नहि भ’ रहल अछि। कोलोराडो नेपाल जकाँ लगैत अछि, पहाड़ देखबा मे अबैत अछि, पैदल ट्रेल सेहो भ’ सकैत अछि।”

हिमचुली केरऽ मतलब होय छै “बर्फी चोटी,” वैसे ।

खगेन्द्र सेहो काफी उद्यमी छथि। अपनऽ नेपाली रेस्टोरेंट के अलावा, हाईलैंड हिमचुली लोकेशन के बगल में स्थित पिज्जा एली के मालिक भी छै, जेकरा में न्यूयॉर्क स्टाइल के पिज्जा परोसलऽ जाय छै ।

जं नेपाली भोजन सं अपरिचित छी तं एतय उल्लेखित तीनू रेस्टोरेंट — हिमचुली, शेर्पा हाउस, याक आ येती — में बुफे अछि जाहि सं अलग-अलग व्यंजन के स्वाद ल सकैत छी.

अरवाडा याक आरू येती केरऽ स्थान १८६४ केरऽ विक्टोरियन युग केरऽ हवेली प॑ छै आरू ओल्ड टाउन अरवाडा स॑ तीन ब्लॉक दूर स्थित छै । शेर्पा हाउस, जे एकटा ऐतिहासिक भवन में सेहो अछि, डाउनटाउन गोल्डन सं दू ब्लॉक दूर अछि. मालिक ल्हकपा शेर्पा एहि संपत्ति के फ्रंट रेंज के नेपाली के सांस्कृतिक केंद्र के रूप मे विकसित केने छथिन्ह. गोल्डन, कोलोराडो में शेरपा हाउस रेस्टोरेंट आ संस्कृति केंद्र मंगल दिन, 28 जनवरी, 2025 के.(फोटो ह्योंग चांग/द डेनवर पोस्ट के)

हमरा लेल त’ बस सुगंध मे किछु खास बात छैक जखन कखनो हम कोनो नेपाली रेस्टोरेंट मे घुसैत छी, लहसुन, अदरक, जीरा, धनिया आ हल्दीक ओहि तीक्ष्ण सुगंध मे साँस लैत छी. मादक भ’ गेलै।

असल में, ई टुकड़ा लिखबाले बैसबा सं पहिने, हम अरवाडा में याक आ यति कें चिकन मोमोक टेकआउट लंच ऑर्डर ले फोन करबाक विरोध नहिं क’ सकलहुं, जकरा ओ सब स्वादिष्ट भारतीय चटनी डिपिंग सॉसक संग परोसैत छथि. बहुत रास याद आबि गेल, जेना सदिखन होइत अछि।

title: Victims of the Nepal floods remembered during North Texas vigil - Yahoo
description: Victims of the Nepal floods remembered during North Texas vigil  Yahoo
publisher.title: Yahoo
full_article:
A North Texas Nepali community gathered in Euless for a candlelight vigil to remember victims of the floods in Nepal. Hundreds of people met outside the Shree Pashupatinath Temple and Bouddha Vihar, where priests led chants and prayers. Gita Pandey, a Euless resident, said several relatives were victims of the floods and their bodies have not been found. She said some relatives were missing at one of the country's hydropower sites, and 55-year-old Ram Chandra Bhatta said his brother-in-law is still missing. The vigil came 13 days after flooding that killed more than 1,300 people in Nepal and Tibet, with about 5,000 still missing. Biraj Paudel, a student at University of Texas at Arlington, said his family is safe, while others in his circle were affected by the disaster.

title: Death toll from Nepal-China border floods rises to 1,410, with thousands still missing - trtworld.com
description: Death toll from Nepal-China border floods rises to 1,410, with thousands still missing  trtworld.com
publisher.title: trtworld.com
full_article:
Nepali authorities have retrieved another 10 bodies in flood-hit areas as the death toll from devastating floods and mudslides that struck the Nepal-China border late last month climbed to 1,410, with over 5,650 still missing, official statistics showed on Wednesday.

Of those missing, 848 are foreigners, according to official figures from both Nepal and China.

Some 1,367 bodies have been recovered from flood-stricken districts in Nepal, while 5,132 people, including 587 foreigners, remain missing, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.

Over 13,600 people have so far been rescued, including as recently as last weekend.

नेपाल आ चीन दुनू देशक आधिकारिक आंकड़ा अनुसार लापता मे सँ ८४८ गोटे विदेशी अछि ।

नेपालके बाढिग्रस्त जिल्लासँ करिब १,३६७ शव बरामद भेल अछि, तहिना ५८७ विदेशी सहित ५,१३२ गोटे लापता रहल नेपालक राष्ट्रिय आपदा जोखिम न्यूनीकरण आ प्रबन्धन प्राधिकरण जनौलक अछि ।

title: Nepal floods: Survivor captures horrifying moment flash floods engulf homes, roads and buildings - The Times of India
description: Nepal floods: Survivor captures horrifying moment flash floods engulf homes, roads and buildings  The Times of India
publisher.title: The Times of India
full_article:
New video of catastrophic Nepal floods surface



Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.



NEW DELHI: A new video from Nepal appears to capture the terrifying moments as flash floodwaters surge through a settlement, sweeping away houses, buildings and parts of a road while people scramble for higher ground. Students can be seen inside what appears to be a school building as the water level of a nearby river rises rapidly.The footage was uploaded on the Facebook page of Nepal7 media outlet and appears to have been recorded from inside a school, where several students are initially seen. Within minutes, floodwaters surge through a stream close to the building, carrying boulders, debris and water, while nearby buildings and a road on which vehicles had been travelling appear to be swept away and submerged. As the torrent intensifies, the person recording the footage and the students move up the stairs inside the building to reach higher ground.The video comes as Nepal continues to deal with the aftermath of devastating flash floods that authorities said had killed 1,356 people by Monday.According to Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), rescue teams were still searching for 4,996 people, including at least 589 foreign nationals.Around 13,400 people had been rescued.The floods were triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, according to authorities. The resulting surge travelled downstream through the Bhotekoshi River, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.The disaster also affected neighbouring Tibet and China. Chinese media reports said at least 43 people were killed on the Chinese side, while more than 500 remained missing in Tibet.NDRRMA said 363 bodies had been recovered in Chitwan, 223 in Nawalparasi East, 221 in Nawalparasi West, 197 in Nuwakot, 169 in Rasuwa, 75 in Gorkha, 70 in Dhading and 38 in Tanahu.Identifying the dead has remained a major challenge. Only 98 bodies had been identified and handed over to families by Monday, according to NDRRMA. Nepal Police has been collecting DNA samples from relatives of missing people to help identify unclaimed remains.More than 1,000 unidentified bodies have been buried after DNA samples were collected for future identification, officials said.Nepal observed a national day of mourning on Monday, marking the continuing toll of the disaster.

title: What 13 minutes in Nepal can teach us about acting before disaster strikes - The New Humanitarian
description: What 13 minutes in Nepal can teach us about acting before disaster strikes  The New Humanitarian
publisher.title: The New Humanitarian
full_article:
Rajendra Dawadi had to make a decision in an instant. Warned that floodwaters were racing towards his school in Nepal’s Trishuli Valley, the headmaster had no way of knowing how much time he had, nor whether the floodwaters would reach his school. He did not hesitate and evacuated more than 900 students and 16 staff to higher ground.

Approximately 13 minutes later, a wall of water, mud, and debris swept through the area, destroying the school.

Dawadi acted before he knew for certain what was coming. His calculation was simple. If the warning proved wrong, his students would miss a day of school. If it was right and he did nothing, hundreds of children could die.

The instinct to act while there is still time, despite uncertainty, is at the heart of anticipatory action. Investing ahead of known risks has been shown to save lives and reduce losses. But acting ahead requires accepting that some forecasts will never provide complete certainty, and that waiting to act can carry far higher consequences.

Nepal shows what formal systems can and cannot do

Nepal is hardly a newcomer to acting ahead of disasters. The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology introduced the flood early warning system in the 1990s, combining both high-tech river level monitoring stations with simpler community-based systems for detecting rising waters and disseminating warnings.

In 2022, the government held the first national dialogue on anticipatory action, and this year endorsed a national policy. Humanitarian organisations have been experimenting with anticipatory approaches for more than a decade, releasing pre-arranged emergency funding at least twice for flood response.

The August disaster, however, fell outside of the mainly weather-related monsoon flooding that these mechanisms were designed to anticipate and warn against. A huge section of glacier and surrounding bedrock collapsed high in Tibet, sending ice, rock, and debris into the river system and generating a catastrophic flood that travelled nearly 100 kilometres downstream. Automatic monitoring stations along the upper Bhotekoshi River were meant to detect rising water and alert communities downstream, but the flood moved so quickly that monitoring stations inside Nepal were destroyed before they could transmit a warning. The community-level river gauges that gradually measured river behaviour were also too slow for a flood travelling at an average speed of 193 kilometres per hour.

Some of these limitations were already understood. A 2023 review of Nepal’s anticipatory action experience raised concerns about the reliability of forecasts and called for greater flexibility to combine scientific triggers with human judgement and changing conditions on the ground. A later study in 2025 found their early warning messaging system frequently did not prompt the necessary actions to save lives and protect assets.

What happened at Dawadi’s school shows why this matters. The warning that saved Dawadi’s students did not come through the formal monitoring or early warning system. A relative upstream called the school accountant. Teachers received calls from family and friends. A parent arrived to collect her child. Dawadi ordered the evacuation. Teachers, parents, and others then helped get the children uphill. Many others were not so fortunate. Elsewhere along the flood’s path, people had almost no time to react.

Forecasting and early warning technology remain essential, but they have to be matched by readiness at the community level – evacuation plans, trusted communication networks, prepared local institutions and people able to act when information arrives.

Those community connections are part of the infrastructure of disaster readiness. I saw their importance when I lived in Japan and studied how the country prepares for disasters in 2019. Japan is famous for its enormous investment in seawalls, flood defences, earthquake-resistant buildings and sophisticated warning systems. But some of its most important investments are far simpler.

Children learn about disaster risk from kindergarten. Communities practise evacuations. Families are encouraged to have a go-bag ready at all times. Residents identify neighbours who may need help. Survivors share their experiences with communities facing similar hazards.

Japan also shows the limits of relying too heavily on infrastructure and more formal warning systems. During severe 2018 flooding in Mabi, a district in western Japan situated near two rivers, embankments were overwhelmed and mobile-phone warnings failed to reach some of the elderly people most at risk. Research after the Mabi flood and the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and Tsunami found that some residents delayed evacuating because they believed physical defences would protect them.

Forecasting and early warning technology remain essential, but they have to be matched by readiness at the community level – evacuation plans, trusted communication networks, prepared local institutions and people able to act when information arrives. These investments may be less visible than satellites, monitoring stations or dams, but they can determine whether a warning actually saves a life.

Schools are an important part of that community readiness. My research on education and anticipatory action with the Geneva Global Hub for Education in Emergencies in 2024 found much the same thing that Dawadi’s experience demonstrates: Schools can play a critical role in turning early warnings into action. They reach children and families every day, while teachers are often trusted community leaders who can communicate risks, organise evacuations, and connect formal warning systems with local knowledge. Disaster education also gives children knowledge they take home and carry into adulthood, strengthening the ability of entire communities to respond to future crises.

Governments, donors, and aid agencies must become more comfortable spending money before they can be certain a crisis will unfold as forecast.

Scientists are still grappling with how to predict rock-ice avalanches like the one in Nepal. But as glacial flooding increases as a result of global warming, they warn that these events are expected to be more common around the world. Anticipatory approaches and funding will need to adapt to include these emerging risks while investing more in the local institutions and relationships that can turn warnings into action.

Yet humanitarian financing still runs overwhelmingly in the opposite direction. Ninety-nine percent of international humanitarian funding still flows after disasters happen and only about 12% of total anticipatory action funding between 2022 and 2023 involved those organisations closest to communities. In a time of collapsing budgets and hyper-prioritisation, it is urgent to rethink whether scarce resources are being deployed where – and when – they can have the greatest effect.

Some actions may prove unnecessary. Sometimes, supplies will be moved for a flood that changes course. Cash may be released ahead of a drought that proves less severe than expected. Schools may close for storms that never arrive. That does not make those decisions bad ones. Governments, donors, and aid agencies must become more comfortable spending money before they can be certain a crisis will unfold as forecast. The cost of acting unnecessarily can be far smaller than the cost of acting too late.

Dawadi understood that tradeoff.
translated:
राजेन्द्र दावादी के पल भर में निर्णय लेबय पड़लनि। नेपालक त्रिशूली उपत्यका मे बाढ़िक पानि हुनकर स्कूल दिस दौड़ि रहल अछि से चेतावनी देलनि, हेडमास्टर केँ ई बुझबाक कोनो उपाय नहि छलनि जे हुनका लग कतेक समय छनि, आ ने बाढ़िक पानि हुनकर स्कूल धरि पहुँचत कि नहि. ओ कोनो संकोच नहि केलनि आ 900 सं बेसी छात्र आ 16 कर्मचारी के ऊँच मैदान पर ल गेलाह.

लगभग 13 मिनट बाद एहि इलाका मे पानि, थाल आ मलबा क देबाल आबि गेल, जाहि स स्कूल तबाह भ गेल।

दावादी ओकरा निश्चित रूपसँ बुझबासँ पहिने काज केलक जे की आबि रहल अछि । हुनकर गणना सरल छलनि। जँ चेतावनी गलत साबित होइत तँ ओकर विद्यार्थी सभ एक दिन स्कूलसँ छूटि जाइत छल । जँ ठीक रहैत आ ओ किछु नहि करितथि तँ सैकड़ो बच्चा मरि सकैत छल ।

अनिश्चितताक बादो समय रहैत काज करबाक वृत्ति पूर्वानुमानात्मक क्रियाक मूल मे होइत छैक । ज्ञात जोखिम सं आगू निवेश सं जान बचाबय आ नुकसान कम करय के बात कहल गेल अछि. लेकिन आगू बढ़ै लेली ई बात क॑ स्वीकार करना जरूरी छै कि कुछ पूर्वानुमान स॑ कहियो पूरा निश्चय नै मिलतै, आरू काम करै के इंतजार करला स॑ एकरऽ परिणाम कहीं अधिक होय सकै छै ।

नेपाल ई देखाबैत अछि जे औपचारिक व्यवस्था की क' सकैत अछि आ की नहि क' सकैत अछि

आपदा स आगू काज करबा मे नेपाल शायदे कोनो नव आगंतुक अछि। जल विज्ञान आरू मौसम विभाग न॑ १९९० के दशक म॑ बाढ़ केरऽ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली शुरू करलकै, जेकरा म॑ बढ़तऽ पानी के पता लगाबै आरू चेतावनी फैलाबै लेली उच्च तकनीक वाला नदी स्तर प॑ निगरानी दूनू स्टेशनऽ क॑ सरल समुदाय आधारित प्रणाली के साथ जोड़लऽ गेलऽ छेलै ।

2022 म॑ सरकार न॑ पूर्वानुमानित कार्रवाई प॑ पहलऽ राष्ट्रीय संवाद करलकै, आरू ई साल एगो राष्ट्रीय नीति के समर्थन करलकै । मानवीय संगठन एक दशक स॑ भी अधिक समय स॑ प्रत्याशित दृष्टिकोण के प्रयोग करी रहलऽ छै, जेकरा म॑ बाढ़ के प्रतिक्रिया लेली कम स॑ कम दू बार पूर्व निर्धारित आपातकालीन फंडिंग जारी करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

अगस्त केरऽ आपदा, हालांकि, मुख्य रूप स॑ मौसम स॑ जुड़लऽ मानसून केरऽ बाढ़ स॑ बाहर गिरी गेलै जेकरऽ पूर्वानुमान आरू चेतावनी लेली ई तंत्रऽ के डिजाइन करलऽ गेलऽ छेलै । तिब्बत में ग्लेशियर आरू आसपास केरऽ बेडरोक केरऽ एगो विशाल खंड ऊँचऽ भाग में गिरी गेलै, जेकरा स॑ बर्फ, चट्टान आरू मलबा नदी प्रणाली में भेजलऽ गेलै आरू एक भयावह बाढ़ पैदा होय गेलै जे लगभग १०० किलोमीटर नीचें गेलै । ऊपरी भोटेकोशी नदी के किनारे स्वचालित निगरानी स्टेशन के उद्देश्य बढ़ैत पानि के पता लगाबय आ नीचा के समुदाय के सचेत करय के छल, मुदा बाढ़ एतेक तेजी सं बढ़ल जे नेपाल के भीतर के निगरानी स्टेशन के चेतावनी संचारित करय सं पहिने नष्ट क देल गेल. समुदाय स्तरीय नदी गेज जे धीरे-धीरे नदी के व्यवहार के मापैत छल, ओ सेहो बहुत धीमा छल जे बाढ़ के औसत गति 193 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा के गति सं चलैत छल.

एहि मे स किछु सीमा पहिने स बुझल गेल छल। नेपाल केरऽ प्रत्याशित कार्य अनुभव केरऽ २०२३ केरऽ समीक्षा म॑ पूर्वानुमान केरऽ विश्वसनीयता के बारे म॑ चिंता पैदा करलऽ गेलै आरू वैज्ञानिक ट्रिगर क॑ मानवीय निर्णय आरू जमीन प॑ बदलतऽ परिस्थिति के साथ जोड़ै लेली अधिक लचीलापन के आह्वान करलऽ गेलै । बाद मँ 2025 मँ एगो अध्ययन मँ पता चललै कि हुनकऽ पूर्व चेतावनी संदेश प्रणाली अक्सर जान बचाबै आरू संपत्ति के सुरक्षा लेली आवश्यक कार्रवाई लेली प्रेरित नै करै छै ।

दावादी’क स्कूल मे जे भेलै से ई दर्शाबै छै कि ई बात कियैक मायने रखै छै. जे चेतावनी दवादी के छात्र के बचा लेलक ओ औपचारिक निगरानी या पूर्व चेतावनी प्रणाली के माध्यम सं नहि आयल छल. अपस्ट्रीम के एकटा रिश्तेदार स्कूल के एकाउंटेंट के फोन केलक। शिक्षक कए परिवार आ मित्र स फोन आयल। एकटा अभिभावक अपन बच्चा के बटोरय लेल पहुंचल। दावादी खाली करबाक आदेश देलनि। तखन शिक्षक, अभिभावक, आ अन्य लोकनि बच्चा सभ केँ चढ़ाबय मे मदद केलनि। कतेको आन लोकक ओतेक सौभाग्य नहि छल। बाढ़ि’क बाट मे आन ठाम लोक केँ प्रतिक्रिया देबाक समय लगभग नहि छल.

पूर्वानुमान आ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रौद्योगिकी आवश्यक बनल छै, मुदा ओकर मिलान समुदाय स्तर पर तत्परता सं करनाय होयत छै – खाली करय कें योजना, विश्वसनीय संचार नेटवर्क, तैयार स्थानीय संस्थान आ जानकारी आवय पर कार्य करय मे सक्षम लोग.

ओ सामुदायिक कनेक्शन आपदा तत्परता कें बुनियादी ढाँचा कें हिस्सा छै. हम जापान में रहैत जखन एकर महत्व देखलहुं आ अध्ययन केलहुं जे 2019 में देश आपदा के तैयारी कोना करैत अछि.जापान समुद्री देवाल, बाढ़ि सं बचाव, भूकंप प्रतिरोधी भवन आ परिष्कृत चेतावनी प्रणाली में अपन भारी निवेश के लेल प्रसिद्ध अछि. मुदा एकर किछु महत्वपूर्ण निवेश कहीं बेसी सरल अछि।

बच्चाक कें बालवाड़ी सं आपदा कें जोखिम कें बारे मे पता चलएयत छै. समुदाय खाली करय के अभ्यास करैत अछि। परिवारक कें प्रोत्साहित कैल जायत छै की हर समय गो-बैग तैयार रहय. निवासी पड़ोसी कें पहचान करएयत छै, जेकरा मदद कें जरूरत भ सकएय छै. बचि गेल लोगक अपन अनुभवक कें ओय समुदायक कें संग साझा करएयत छै जे समान खतरा कें सामना करएयत छै.

जापान बुनियादी ढाँचा आरू अधिक औपचारिक चेतावनी प्रणाली प॑ बहुत जादा भरोसा करै के सीमा भी देखाबै छै । 2018 म॑ पश्चिमी जापान केरऽ एगो जिला माबी म॑ दू नदी के पास स्थित भयंकर बाढ़ के दौरान तटबंधऽ प॑ भारी पड़लऽ छेलै आरू मोबाइल-फोन के चेतावनी सबस॑ बेसी खतरा म॑ पड़लऽ कुछ बुजुर्ग लोगऽ तलक नै पहुँची सकलऽ छेलै । माबी बाढ़ आरू २०११ केरऽ महान पूर्वी जापान भूकंप आरू सुनामी के बाद के शोध म॑ पता चललै कि कुछ निवासी न॑ घरऽ स॑ बाहर निकलै म॑ देरी करलकै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरा मानना ​​छेलै कि भौतिक रक्षा स॑ ओकरऽ सुरक्षा मिलतै ।

पूर्वानुमान आ पूर्व चेतावनी प्रौद्योगिकी आवश्यक बनल छै, मुदा ओकर मिलान समुदाय स्तर पर तत्परता सं करनाय होयत छै – खाली करय कें योजना, विश्वसनीय संचार नेटवर्क, तैयार स्थानीय संस्थान आ जानकारी आवय पर कार्य करय मे सक्षम लोग. ई निवेश उपग्रह, निगरानी स्टेशन या बांध के तुलना म॑ कम दिखाई द॑ सकै छै, लेकिन ई ई तय करी सकै छै कि चेतावनी स॑ वास्तव म॑ जान बचै छै कि नै ।

स्कूल ओहि सामुदायिक तत्परता के एकटा महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा अछि. 2024 म॑ जेनेवा ग्लोबल हब फॉर एजुकेशन इन इमरजेंसी के साथ शिक्षा आरू प्रत्याशित कार्रवाई प॑ हमरऽ शोध म॑ बहुत कुछ वू ही मिललै जे दावादी केरऽ अनुभव स॑ पता चलै छै कि स्कूल जल्दी चेतावनी क॑ कार्रवाई म॑ बदलै म॑ अहम भूमिका निभा सकै छै । इ हर दिन बच्चाक आ परिवारक तइक पहुंचएयत छै, जखन कि शिक्षक अक्सर भरोसेमंद समुदायक कें नेता होयत छै जे जोखिम कें संवाद कयर सकएय छै, निकासी कें आयोजन कयर सकएय छै, आ औपचारिक चेतावनी प्रणाली कें स्थानीय ज्ञान सं जोड़ सकएय छै. आपदा शिक्षा बच्चाक कें ओ ज्ञान कें सेहो देयत छै जे ओ घर ल जायत छै आ वयस्कता मे ल जायत छै, जे भविष्य कें संकट कें जवाब देवय कें लेल पूरा समुदायक कें क्षमता कें मजबूत करयत छै.

सरकार, दाता, आ सहायता एजेंसी कें पैसा खर्च करय मे बेसि सहज होनाय आवश्यक छै, ओकरा सं पहिले कि ओ इ निश्चिंत भ सकय कि कोनों संकट पूर्वानुमान कें अनुसार खुलतय.

वैज्ञानिक एखनो एहि बात सं जूझि रहल छथिन्ह जे नेपाल मे जेना चट्टान-बर्फ के हिमस्खलन के भविष्यवाणी कोना कएल जाए. लेकिन जेना-जेना ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के परिणामस्वरूप हिमनदीय बाढ़ बढ़ी रहलऽ छै, वू चेतावनी दै छै कि ई घटना दुनिया भर म॑ अधिक होय के उम्मीद छै । प्रत्याशित दृष्टिकोण आ वित्तपोषण कें इ उभरैत जोखिम कें शामिल करय कें लेल अनुकूलित करय कें जरूरत होयत आ स्थानीय संस्थाक आ संबंधक मे बेसि निवेश करय कें होयत जे चेतावनी कें कार्यवाही मे बदल सकय छै.

तइयो मानवीय वित्तपोषण एखनो भारी मात्रा मे एकर विपरीत दिशा मे चलि रहल अछि। अंतरराष्ट्रीय मानवीय वित्तपोषण कें 99 प्रतिशत आपदाक कें बाद अखनी तइक बहय छै आ 2022 सं 2023 कें बीच कुल प्रत्याशित कार्यवाही कें वित्तपोषण कें मात्र लगभग 12% समुदायक कें सब सं नजदीकी संगठनक कें शामिल कैल गेलय. बजट केरऽ पतन आरू अति-प्राथमिकता केरऽ समय म॑ ई बात प॑ पुनर्विचार करना जरूरी छै कि दुर्लभ संसाधनऽ क॑ कहाँ – आरू कहिया – सबसें जादा प्रभाव डाल॑ सकै छै, तैनात करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै कि नै ।

किछु काज अनावश्यक साबित भ सकैत अछि। कखनो काल, बाढ़ि लेल आपूर्ति स्थानांतरित भ जायत जे मार्ग बदलि जायत। सूखा सं पहिने नकदी जारी भ सकैत अछि जे उम्मीद सं कम गंभीर साबित भ जाएत. स्कूल बंद भ सकैत अछि जे आंधी-तूफान कहियो नहि आबि सकैत अछि। जे ओहि निर्णय सभकेँ खराब नहि बना दैत अछि । सरकार, दाता, आ सहायता एजेंसी कें पैसा खर्च करय मे बेसि सहज होनाय आवश्यक छै, ओकरा सं पहिले कि ओ इ निश्चिंत भ सकय कि कोनों संकट पूर्वानुमान कें अनुसार खुलतय. अनावश्यक रूप स अभिनय करबाक लागत बहुत देर स अभिनय करबाक लागत स कहीं कम भ सकैत अछि।

दावादी ओ ट्रेडऑफ बुझि गेल।

title: Nepal seeks survivors two weeks after deadly floods - fox26medford.com
description: Nepal seeks survivors two weeks after deadly floods  fox26medford.com
publisher.title: fox26medford.com
full_article:
Nepali rescuers clung to hopes of finding survivors trapped in hydropower tunnels on Wednesday, two weeks after deadly flooding triggered by a glacial mountain collapse.

The August 26 tsunami-like surge of water, mud and debris, which began on the China-Nepal border, has killed more than 1,410 people and left 5,651 missing.

"The rescue and search work in the tunnels at Trishuli 3A, 3B and Chilime hydropower projects is ongoing," Nepal Army spokesman Raja Ram Basnet told AFP.

In Nepal, 1,367 bodies have been recovered and 5,132 people are missing, its disaster authority said on Wednesday.

In China, 43 people are dead and 519 are missing, according to state media.

Hundreds of foreigners are among the missing, as well as hundreds of hydropower workers.

Three people were rescued from deep inside tunnels -- two Nepalis on Friday and a Chinese man on Saturday.

But there has been no official confirmation of further survivors since then.

Thousands of people displaced by the disaster are living in camps, and the charity Save the Children said as many as 540 children had been separated from their parents.

Nepal police said they were taking extra care to ensure the safety of children and women in relief camps.

"We have become more vigilant in temporary holding centres in the affected areas where there are children, women or minority groups who could be victims of sexual abuse," said Nepal Police spokesman Abi Narayan Kafle.

"We have also started providing psychosocial counselling in different camps," he told AFP.

While the exact cause of the glacial collapse is unclear, climate change is accelerating glacial melt worldwide and increasing the risk of such disasters.

Nepal, a largely rural nation of 30 million people that has contributed little to the greenhouse gas emissions driving global warming, has said reconstruction could cost billions of dollars.

Kafle said security personnel have involved community members to search for bodies feared buried under debris.

"We have started a special search campaign for missing bodies all across the Bhotekoshi river corridor," he said.

"We are also using drones to search for bodies."
